name: Whist Romanian
description: Romanian Whist is an exact-prediction trick-taking game for 3 to 6 players. Each player bids how many tricks they will take; the sum of all bids must not equal the number of cards dealt. Players score for making their contract exactly and lose points for over- or undertricks.

overview.description: Romanian Whist is an exact-prediction trick-taking game for 3 to 6 players. Each player bids how many tricks they will take; the sum of all bids must not equal the number of cards dealt. Players score for making their contract exactly and lose points for over- or undertricks.

history.origins: Romanian Whist is a regional exact-prediction trick game; known in Romania simply as Whist. Description contributed by Werner Hintze and others.
timeline: 20th century: Documented as regional Romanian exact-prediction game; related to Oh Hell.

setup.players: Three to six players, each playing alone (no partnerships). Best with 4 to 6.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck; 8 cards per player in use (24 for 3 players, 32 for 4, up to 48 for 6).
setup.dealing: First dealer chosen at random; deal rotates clockwise. Number of cards per player varies by deal: starts at 1 card each for as many deals as players, increases by one per deal up to 8 each, then 8 each for as many deals as players, then decreases back to 1. Example with 4 players: 1,1,1,1, 2,3,4,5,6,7, 8,8,8,8, 7,6,5,4,3,2, 1,1,1,1 (24 deals). After the deal, the next card is turned for trump; in 8-card hands no card remains, so those hands are played without trumps.

rules.objective: Win exactly the number of tricks you bid each hand. Score 5 plus tricks made when you make your contract; lose 1 point per trick over or under your bid. Highest total score after the full deal sequence wins.
rules.gameplay: Each hand: dealer deals the current hand size (1 to 8 cards per player). Next card is turned for trump (except in 8-card hands, which are no-trump). In order from dealer's left, each player bids how many tricks they will take; the sum of all bids must not equal the number of cards per player. Player to dealer's left leads; follow suit if possible, otherwise play trump if possible, else discard. Highest trump wins the trick, or highest card of the led suit if no trump. Trick winner leads. After all tricks are played, score: make contract = 5 + tricks made; miss = minus 1 per trick difference.
keyRules: Bid exact number of tricks; sum of all bids must not equal cards per player.
Follow suit; if unable, must trump if possible; else discard any card.
Trump determined by turned card after deal; 8-card hands are no-trump.
Making contract scores 5 plus tricks; each overtrick or undertrick costs 1 point.

strategy.basic: Track which cards have been played; count trumps and high cards to estimate whether you can make your bid. On 1-card hands, bid based on your single card and position.

variations.name: 8-1-8 deal sequence
variations.description: Begin and end with 8-card hands (8,8,8,8, then 7 down to 1, then back up to 8,8,8,8); reduces 1-card luck.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal sequence change only; engine deal pattern override not yet modeled.

variations.name: Blind 1-card
variations.description: On 1-card deals everyone bids before looking at their card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bid-before-looking affects bid phase only; no engine overrides encoded yet.

variations.name: Forehead 1-card
variations.description: Players hold 1-card on forehead; see others' cards, bid accordingly.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Visibility and bid timing differ; engine overrides for this variant not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Make contract: 5 points plus number of tricks made. Miss: lose 1 point per trick over or under bid. Highest total after full deal sequence wins.
scoring.winCondition: Highest total score after the full sequence of deals (1-up-to-8-down-to-1).
